Stability Landscape Along the Program or a Covariate

Source: R/stability_landscape.R
landscape_trend.Rd

The landscape of stability_landscape() traced along a second axis. The axis is either the program phase, along = "phase": the landscape is estimated from the transitions inside a sliding window of window time steps; or a numeric per-sequence covariate such as a grade, along = "grade": at each value of the covariate it comes from the k nearest sequences, weighted by a tricube kernel (Cleveland 1979). Intervals come from resampling whole sequences.

Two heights are available. depth = "stay" (default) is the depth of stability_landscape(), the log of each state's expected stay, \(-\log(1 - P_{ii})\). depth = "occupancy" is the quasi-potential \(-\log \pi_i\) of the stationary distribution, with ridges at \(-\log\) of the symmetrised probability flux \((\pi_i P_{ij} + \pi_j P_{ji}) / 2\) between neighbouring states (Wang et al. 2008): a low cup is a state the process spends much of its time in, a high ridge a switch it rarely makes.

Usage

landscape_trend(
  x,
  along = "phase",
  depth = c("stay", "occupancy"),
  states = NULL,
  window = 5L,
  k = 30L,
  n_grid = 20L,
  iter = 500L,
  ci_level = 0.95,
  seed = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'net_landscape_trend'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'net_landscape_trend'
print(x, digits = 2, ...)

# S3 method for class 'net_landscape_trend'
plot(x, type = c("lines", "surface"), theta = 10, phi = 30, ...)

Arguments

x

A transition network from build_network() (method "relative" or "frequency"), a grouped one, or a wide sequence data frame. A covariate is read from the network's metadata, which build_network() fills with the numeric columns of a wide data frame. For the print() and plot() methods: an object of class net_landscape_trend.

along

"phase" (default), or the name of a numeric per-sequence covariate.

depth

"stay" (default) or "occupancy", see above.

states

Character vector naming every state once, in drawing order. Default: alphabetical.

window

Integer. With along = "phase": time steps per window. Default 5.

k

Integer. With a covariate: nearest sequences per slice. Default 30 (capped at the number of sequences).

n_grid

Integer. With a covariate: slices between its 5th and 95th percentile, with the full range used if these coincide. Default 20.

iter

Integer. Bootstrap resamples of sequences. Default 500.

ci_level

Numeric in (0, 1). Interval level. Default 0.95.

seed

Integer or NULL. Seed for the resampling, scoped to the call.

object

A net_landscape_trend object (for summary()).

...

Ignored.

digits

Integer. Decimal places in print(). Default 2.

type

In plot(): "lines" (default), one line per state with its interval band; or "surface", a 3D persp() landscape with the states across and the second axis in depth, one panel per network on a shared height scale.

theta, phi

Numeric. In plot(type = "surface"): viewing angles.

Value

An object of class "net_landscape_trend".

In summary(): a data frame with one row per network, position and feature: group, along, value (window centre or covariate value), label (window steps or value), feature ("well", or "ridge" with depth = "occupancy"), state (a state, or two for a ridge), the height (depth for "stay", potential for "occupancy"), ci_lower, ci_upper, dwell ("stay" only) and n_from (transitions out of the state in the window, or their weighted sum in the slice; wells only).

In print(): x, invisibly.

In plot(): with type = "lines" a ggplot object; with type = "surface" x, invisibly, after drawing.

Details

Network input replays per-sequence weighting, concatenation and boundary markers. Concatenated sequences are the resampling units. With a covariate, its value must be constant within each concatenated unit. Scaled, thresholded or otherwise modified networks whose weights do not match their stored sequences are refused; pass the original sequences to estimate a new landscape. Observed shares count prepared positions without sequence weighting. Phase windows retain the full sequence's weight.

With depth = "stay", a window or slice in which a state is never left gives an infinite depth, and one in which it does not occur gives NA. With depth = "occupancy", a window whose chain has no unique stationary distribution is NA throughout. Such points are kept in summary(), left out of the lines and the surface, and counted in the plot caption. Interval bands are clipped at the panel edge, which is set by the estimates. Consecutive windows share all but one step and neighbouring slices most of their sequences, so neighbouring points are not independent.

Errors

nestimate_not_markov; nestimate_bad_input for an unknown, non-numeric or constant covariate, bad states, or a window longer than the sequences; nestimate_landscape_unestimable for fewer than five usable sequences.

References

Cleveland, W. S. (1979). Robust locally weighted regression and smoothing scatterplots. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 74, 829–836.

Kramers, H. A. (1940). Brownian motion in a field of force and the diffusion model of chemical reactions. Physica, 7, 284–304.

Wang, J., Xu, L., & Wang, E. (2008). Potential landscape and flux framework of nonequilibrium networks. PNAS, 105, 12271–12276.

See also

stability_landscape, landscape_surface

Examples

net <- build_network(trajectories, method = "relative")
trend <- landscape_trend(net, along = "phase",
  states = c("Disengaged", "Average", "Active"), iter = 50, seed = 1)
trend
#> Stability landscape along program phase (5-step windows): 3 states, 1 network, 50 resamples
#> 
#> Cup depth (log of the expected stay; higher = more stable) at the two ends and its range:
#>       state first at_first  last at_last  min  max
#>  Disengaged   1-5     0.72 11-15    0.89 0.42 1.01
#>     Average   1-5     0.98 11-15    1.10 0.77 1.10
#>      Active   1-5     1.31 11-15    1.29 1.03 1.32
# \donttest{
plot(trend)

occupancy <- landscape_trend(net, depth = "occupancy", window = 6,
  states = c("Disengaged", "Average", "Active"), iter = 50, seed = 1)
plot(occupancy, type = "surface")

# }
